findings.issue: Accepted contextual limitation. Où can turn the trees into the location of the branches, but the intended possessive relative is more idiomatic and specifically means whose / deren.
findings.recommendation: Optional future replacement for où would remove this alternate locative interpretation.

findings.issue: Accepted staging variation. Depuis son ouverture appears incidentally in a response one lesson before the explicit duration instruction; the modeled and assessed core stays comparative. The route change provides an implicit reason.
findings.recommendation: No edit needed for this path-level stage.

findings.issue: During the holidays can be interpreted as the festive season in American English rather than a vacation. The intended past routine is clear.

lessonsRead.observation: Faisais marks the shopping routine and croisais contrasts clearly with present-day voit.
Pendant mon enfance avoids gender agreement, and suivais transfers to a swimming class. The early title and image reveal the willows.
The conversation explains the family ritual’s value, but one German term describes acquiring the habit rather than having it.
Venait and rentrions test different persons; the cousin supplies new information after the initial tennis recollection.
Ne … plus correctly contrasts present and past play; the later response explains how new players were included.
Fréquentais takes a direct object. The bus schedule explains the change after moving.
Davantage de + noun compares time outdoors, but the learner’s follow-up uses the next stage’s depuis and leaves the reason for walking implicit.
Ça fait trois mois que + present describes an ongoing habit. The German build chunk instead means three months ago.
Depuis que + present is correctly explained. Accepting deliveries gives the requested concrete example beyond the garden.
The market memory uses imparfait for the original scene and a duration with present for today’s familiarity.

findings.issue: The title names the willows and the picture describes their low branches over the river before the friend asks what image the learner remembers. Together they supply the intended answer.
findings.recommendation: Use a neutral childhood school-route title and a river path without identifiable trees or branches.

findings.issue: Où can introduce a place relative with a tree as location: les saules où les branches touchaient presque l’eau. It is less precise than possessive dont but yields a defensible description of which trees are remembered.
findings.recommendation: Remove où as a fallback foil or reframe the relative with an unambiguously possessive antecedent.

findings.issue: wir machten es uns zur Gewohnheit zu means we made it a habit and is incomplete/unnatural as a standalone gloss. The French states an existing habit.
findings.recommendation: Use wir pflegten … zu or wir hatten die Angewohnheit, … zu.

findings.issue: The hints regarder (sans + Infinitiv) and rentrer (pour + Infinitiv) print the exact answers to their own typed blanks.
findings.recommendation: Prompt with the intended meaning or an inflected French form; do not display the missing infinitive.

findings.issue: I see you walking every evening since … needs the present perfect. The image gives away the footbridge. The answer repeats the time since opening, introducing depuis productively one lesson early, without saying how the route makes walking easier.
findings.recommendation: Use I’ve seen you walking … since … and remove the footbridge from the image. A follow-up like Oui, maintenant le chemin est plus court, alors je rentre plus souvent à pied gives the requested reason and preserves L7 comparative staging.

findings.issue: Es ist drei Monate her, dass ich … describes an elapsed interval since an event, the opposite of the continuing habit the exercise specifically teaches.
findings.recommendation: Use chunks that translate ça fait trois mois que as seit drei Monaten and then resegment je laisse la voiture … so the DE/EN glosses reconstruct the ongoing reading.

findings.issue: The learner can write car le verre pèse lourd in the exact same slot as parce que, preserving register, grammar, causal meaning and both translations. No cue distinguishes them.
findings.recommendation: If exact single-answer is required, print the causal conjunction and blank pèse (peser, le verre) instead, or blank que as part of a differently constrained form.

findings.issue: Eine alte Nachbarin typically denotes an elderly neighbor, while former neighbour / ancienne cour establishes a former neighbor.
